clue.text: Organising an insurrection which is getting out of hand

definitions.meaning: read literally, to be in charge of a rebellion is to be running a riot
the idiom for behaving wildly and without control

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is the phrase taken literally, running in the sense of managing; the second is its everyday idiomatic meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means acting without restraint, while the literal reading is managing an uprising; both senses share the phrase.

clue.text: Fashionable doctor confronts artist in shadow

parts.note: U means upper-class, hence socially acceptable or fashionable
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A trendy physician meets a painter in a dark place.
explanation.definitionFit: The darkest central part of a shadow, as in an eclipse, has this Latin name.

clue.text: Just due to get a set of Meissen

indicators.note: set suggests the letters are arranged or placed in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is owed a set of fine Meissen porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a set of Meissen' looks like a china service; Meissen is the German porcelain maker, and its letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Retribution that is deserved, a downfall one has earned, is what Greek tradition personified as a goddess of vengeance.

clue.text: Minority finding no silver in Teesside

indicators.note: the other pieces are placed inside the abbreviation for the region

parts.note: Teesside is in north-east England, abbreviated NE
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A minority group without any silver, living on Teesside.
explanation.walkthrough: Teesside is the area around the River Tees in north-east England. Minority here is the legal sense, being under age.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal minority is the period before adulthood, being under age.

clue.text: Tories get away immediately

parts.note: the Tories are the political Right
to be off is to leave or get away

explanation.definitionFit: Done at once, without delay, as in knowing something straight away.

clue.text: Best for Timothy and Albert to pursue work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
Al is short for Albert

explanation.surface: Two men named Timothy and Albert chasing after a job is ideal.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimal means the most favourable, the ideal or finest.

clue.text: Eccentric seaman takes the lead

definitions.meaning: a character is an eccentric and the main is the sea, so a sea-going oddity
the leading figure in a story or play

explanation.walkthrough: Main is old poetic language for the open sea, and a character is an odd person, so the first part is a whimsical reading of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The protagonist of a story is its central figure, and a seafaring oddball is a character of the main.

clue.text: Mishandle mixture of metal and car

indicators.note: a mixture is a blend, so the letters of the two words are stirred together

parts.note: the setter's slip: the printed word should be tar, the black road-surfacing pitch, whose letters complete the anagram

explanation.surface: Mixing metal and tar is handling them badly.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the clue says 'car', but the anagram needs TAR: METAL plus TAR gives the eight letters, and the answer has no C.
explanation.definitionFit: To abuse or treat roughly is to handle cruelly.

clue.text: Manage to acquire a woman and live in harmony

parts.note: to get on is to manage or cope
to get is to acquire
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Someone manages to win a woman and they live happily together.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on good terms and coexist without quarrels is to rub along well.

clue.text: Give a pound to a beggar for a book

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra
a bum is a tramp or beggar

explanation.surface: Someone hands a pound coin to a beggar in exchange for a book.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a bound volume for photographs or stamps, a kind of book.

clue.text: An awful ordeal for Black Bess?

definitions.meaning: Black Bess was the highwayman Dick Turpin's horse, a dark female horse ridden after dark

explanation.walkthrough: Dick Turpin was a famous English highwayman of legend; his mare Black Bess carried him on night rides, so she is a mare of the night. The question mark flags the punning second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreadful experience is commonly called a living horror dream, and Black Bess is literally a mare that worked by dark.

clue.text: Listeners in hours of darkness have poor vision

indicators.note: the listeners are placed inside the hours of darkness, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: the hours of darkness make up the night
ears are the organs we listen with

explanation.surface: People who listen out at night find they cannot see well.
explanation.definitionFit: To be short-sighted is to have poor distance vision; the phrase is treated as a verb, people who are short-sighted.

clue.text: In some trouble underground

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters of some trouble, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Someone is in a spot of bother below ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A city's underground railway is called by this name in Paris and many other cities.

clue.text: Husky-voiced runner

indicators.note: voiced means spoken out, so the word for a runner is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a racehorse is a runner in a race

explanation.surface: A runner with a rough, throaty voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husky-voiced' reads as one adjective, but the hyphen splits: 'Husky' is the definition and 'voiced' signals that the racing runner is said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A husky voice is rough and croaky, the same as one that is strained and gruff.

clue.text: No problems despite a raging tempest

definitions.meaning: in a storm the sea is entirely rough

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a pun: in a raging storm the sea is nothing but swell, read as one phrase that means everything is fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Everything is satisfactory, the cry of a watchman reporting that nothing is amiss.

clue.text: A French leader articulate and wealthy

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here the start of French

parts.note: an articulate speaker is fluent

explanation.surface: A French political leader who is both eloquent and rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well off is rich, having plenty of money.

clue.text: Senior officer longing to get tuition

parts.note: CO is Commanding Officer
aching means yearning or longing

explanation.surface: A commanding officer eager to receive instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Coaching is private instruction or training, a form of teaching.

clue.text: Account for one of the family

definitions.meaning: a narration or telling of events
a relative by blood or marriage

explanation.definitionFit: A narrative telling is an old sense of the word, and a kinsman is the commoner sense.

clue.text: Hill overlooking Canadian city

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
a window overlooking a garden looks onto it

explanation.surface: A hill with a view over a city in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a rocky hilltop of the kind found on English moors.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Ontario, Canada's largest city.

clue.text: Paper's stock phrase for the plebs

parts.note: rag is a slang term for a low-quality newspaper
a tag is a well-worn quotation or saying

explanation.surface: A newspaper's favourite cliché for describing the common people.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link meaning 'has'. Ragtag, as in ragtag and bobtail, is the rabble.
explanation.definitionFit: The ragtag is a contemptuous term for the common rabble, the lower orders.

clue.text: Is it possible for me to be good-humoured?

parts.note: the first person of to be, turned into a question, gives am I
able means possible or capable

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they can manage to be cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: The question reads as can I, split into AM I and ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A friendly, pleasant disposition is a genial, good-natured one.

clue.text: Aim to find a camper's location

definitions.meaning: a camper sleeps under canvas, inside a tent

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is read as two words: where a camper is, under canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: A purpose or goal is one sense; split in two it says where a camper sleeps.

clue.text: Shrink from a creditor about to become a debtor

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
a debtor is one who owes, an ower

explanation.surface: Someone who was owed money recoils on finding they now owe instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink back in fear is to cringe or quail.

clue.text: A lot of countries exercising restraint

definitions.meaning: a large landmass such as Europe or Africa holds many nations
showing self-control, especially sexual or bodily

explanation.definitionFit: A great landmass holds many nations, and a self-controlled person is abstinent; one word carries both senses.

clue.text: Time to get a literary patroness

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: It is time for a woman to sponsor writers.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the nine Muses, the goddesses who inspire the arts; this one presides over love poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muse of lyric and love poetry is a divine inspirer of writers.

clue.text: Eurasian rose in elegant setting

indicators.note: setting means arranging or placing anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rose from Europe and Asia displayed in a stylish arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in elegant setting' looks like a description of the rose; the letters IN and ELEGANT are rearranged instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweetbriar is a wild rose of Europe and Asia, known poetically by this name.

clue.text: Brushwood can bring car to a halt

definitions.meaning: a thicket or tangle of undergrowth

definitions.text: can bring car to a halt
definitions.meaning: the device that stops a vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: A thicket of undergrowth is one old sense, and the stopping device on a vehicle is the other.

clue.text: Rosemary's message contains a small bloomer

definitions.meaning: rosemary is the herb of remembrance, so its message is a plea to be remembered
a little flower, a plant that blooms

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rosemary' looks like a woman's name, but it is the herb, traditionally for remembrance; 'bloomer' is a flower, not a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: The small blue flower is named for a plea to be remembered, the very message the herb of remembrance sends.
